name: Diffuse Palmoplantar Keratoderma, Bothnian Type

ethnicAssociations: Northern European populations, especially Swedish and Finnish

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Bothnian Type Diffuse Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Diffuse, yellowish hyperkeratosis of the palms and soles with a spongy, white appearance upon water immersion
Onset of symptoms in early childhood, typically before age 10
Histological findings showing hyperkeratosis with epidermolytic changes and spongiosis
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Transient white spongy swelling of affected skin after water immersion

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of diffuse palmoplantar hyperkeratosis with early onset plus histopathological confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but causative gene not definitively identified.

searchTerms: thickened skin on palms and soles
rough skin on hands and feet
chronic athlete's foot or nail fungus

laboratory: Histopathology showing hyperkeratosis with epidermolytic changes and spongiosis
genetic: No definitive causative gene identified; suspected autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
other: Positive water immersion test demonstrating transient white spongy swelling

distinguishingFeatures: Nail dystrophy more prominent and early
Mutations in keratin genes (KRT6A, KRT16, KRT17)

redFlags: Rapid progression of hyperkeratosis with ulceration
Development of constricting bands leading to autoamputation
Signs of secondary infection with systemic symptoms
references: Hovnanian A. Palmoplantar keratodermas: clinical and molecular classification. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2017.
Orphanet: Diffuse palmoplantar keratoderma, Bothnian type - ORPHA:2337
Smith FJD, et al. The molecular basis of palmoplantar keratoderma. Br J Dermatol. 2019.
